arguments.premise_synthesis: The Federal Reserve will reinvest all principal payments from agency securities into Treasury bills starting December 1st. Bond prices and yields are inversely correlated. Reduced demand for mortgage-backed securities puts downward pressure on MBS prices and upward pressure on mortgage rates. Increased demand for Treasury bills puts upward pressure on T-bill prices and downward pressure on T-bill yields. Taken together, this policy lowers Treasury bill yields to benefit government borrowing while raising mortgage rates, harming homeowners.
arguments.conclusion_supported: The Federal Reserve's reinvestment of agency securities principal into Treasury bills is a covert form of quantitative easing that supports government borrowing by lowering yields on short-term government debt, while simultaneously harming the housing market through higher mortgage rates.
